name: Domino Rounce
description: Domino Rounce is a competitive trick-taking game for 2 to 4 players, played with a double-six set of dominoes. Similar to the card game Rounce, players start with a positive score and compete to reduce it to zero by winning tricks. It features a unique 'dummy' hand and high-penalty mechanics for failing to win tricks.

history.origins: Rounce is a German-American variation of the 17th-century game Loo. The domino adaptation was popular in American social clubs in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
timeline: 1800s: Card game Rounce becomes a popular 'countdown' variant of Loo.
Late 1800s: Domino adaptation documented in American gaming guides.
Modern Era: Continues to be played in niche trick-taking circles.
history.cultural: Commonly associated with German-American heritage in the Midwest USA.
history.evolution: Unlike Domino Loo, Rounce transitioned from a pot-based gambling game to a point-based race to zero, which changed the strategic priority from greed to avoidance of penalties.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 5 tiles. A 'dummy' hand of extra tiles is dealt. The player to the right of the dealer turns up a tile to determine the trump suit.

rules.objective: Each player starts with 15 points. Players subtract 1 point for each trick they win; if all except the dealer pass, the dealer subtracts 5 without play. A player who stays in but wins no tricks is rounced and adds 5 to their score; a player who drops out neither gains nor loses. The first to reach or pass zero points wins the game.
rules.gameplay:
1. Folding: After seeing their tiles and trumps, players can 'fold' and sit out the round to avoid penalties.
2. The Dummy: A player can choose to play by discarding their hand and taking the 'dummy' hand.
3. Trick Play: Lead any tile. Must follow suit. If unable to follow, you can play ANY tile (no requirement to trump unless you wish to).
4. Winning: Highest trump wins. If no trump, highest of led suit wins.
keyRules: Blank is the lowest rank (0), 6 is the highest (6).
One end of the tile determines the 'suit', the other its rank.
The winner of a trick must lead a trump next if they hold one.

strategy.basic: If your hand has fewer than two trumps and no 'safe' doubles (like 6-6), folding is the optimal move.
strategy.intermediate: Use the dummy hand only if you are already at a high score (e.g., 12+) since the risk of being rounced is mitigated by the potential for a fresh 5-tile set.
strategy.advanced: Defensive play: If you are close to 0, play conservatively to avoid being rounced, which could set you back multiple rounds.
tips: Counting the 7 tiles of the trump suit is vital. Once four are out, your medium-value trump becomes a high-value one.
Lead high trumps early to flush out opponent trumps.
